findings.reason: The explicit shock and chord construction benefit materially from a paired spacetime/flux picture: the first locates the two states relative to the moving discontinuity, and the second makes the Rankine–Hugoniot speed and convex chord visible. Original standalone tiles show no illustration; this is an explanatory addition, not a defect in the independent proof.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Spacetime panel for the explicitly stated u_L=1,u_R=0 example, t>=0; horizontal x, vertical t.
relations: Shock segment runs from (0,0) to (1.6,3.2), so x/t=1/2 throughout its positive-time part. It illustrates the finite viewing window of x=t/2, not termination of the ray.
Left labels at (-1.1,2) and (-1.1,1.5) lie in x<t/2; right labels at (2,1.2) and (2,0.7) lie in x>t/2.
The origin is the initial jump; no value is prescribed on the shock.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement and proof step 3.1 explicitly give x=t/2, state 1 on the left and state 0 on the right. Step 1.1 computes s=(1+0)/2.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Flux panel: u maps to f(u)=u^2/2 on the displayed u>=0 window, with solid chord endpoints (0,0) and (1,1/2).
relations: The sampled parabola is exactly y=u^2/2. The dashed chord joins the two displayed flux points, slope (1/2-0)/(1-0)=1/2.
On 0<=u<=1, chord minus flux is u(1-u)/2>=0; both endpoints coincide.
The derivative values f'(0)=0 and f'(1)=1 bracket the chord slope 1/2 as stated in the caption.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Local F3 gives f'(u)=u and strict convexity; proof steps 1.1 and 2.1 identify chord speed and admissibility. No new hypothesis or supplier used.
